X.note: The wall has the richest stone, weathering and waterline staining, but it looks like photogrammetry. The cliff-like parapet is a lumpy, melted ramp, and there are dark gaps and white sliver artifacts at the right corner and the left wall. The deck is a flat brown noisy texture. The surrounding buildings are untextured grey boxes. The texture stays fixed across frames.

Y.note: This is the cleanest and most coherent version. The wall is a believable pale limestone with a crenellated parapet, embrasures and small cannon. The gravel deck has varied patches and the lighting is consistent. The surrounding blocks are still untextured grey boxes. The wall is a little over-bright and clean, and the cannon are barely visible. It is stable across frames.

Z.note: The wall is smooth, plasticky white with almost no stone detail, and it reads as a CG mock-up. The deck is a uniform dark asphalt-like noise texture that looks like modern tarmac. Lighting is soft and clean. Stable across frames, but the surrounding buildings are the same blank boxes.

why: Y has the most believable stone, a coherent parapet and gravel deck, and no render breakage, while Z is blank and plasticky with an asphalt-like deck, and X has visible geometry and texture errors.
anachronisms_seen: asphalt-like tarmac deck (Z, and the dark road in all three)
untextured modern-looking grey block buildings behind the bastion (all)
curb-like pale edging along the road (Y, Z)
